guide: Mailbox posts on this page cost between $75 and $250. The selection includes wooden styles in cedar or dark cedar, as well as painted metal finishes such as classic white, onyx black, and stone gray.

Wooden posts are typically made from cedar, which resists rot naturally, while metal posts are often powder-coated for durability and weather resistance. Many items are sold as a post-and-mailbox kit, so the mailbox attaches directly to the post.

When picking a post, consider the height-standard residential posts are 48-54 inches tall-and the style that matches your home’s exterior. Look for sturdy mounting hardware and a concrete base for stable installation.
Check if the kit includes a mailbox that fits your local postal regulations, and verify that the finish is UV-protected to maintain its appearance over time.

faq.answer: Standard residential posts are usually 48-54 inches tall; select a height that matches your mailbox and local guidelines.

faq.answer: Cedar and treated wood are naturally resistant to rot, and painted finishes add extra protection against the elements.
faq.question: Are wooden posts weather-resistant?

faq.answer: Most posts come with a concrete base or mounting hardware that can be set in a pre-drilled hole and secured with concrete or a ground sleeve.
faq.question: How is a post installed?

faq.answer: Many of these kits include a mailbox that attaches to the post, but always verify the product description to be sure.
